releases.fragment_template:
# Skills-first development stack

Start with `.agents/skills/skills-first-start/SKILL.md` for task routing and
orientation. This project records sources in `.skills-first/bundle.lock.json`.
Superpowers supplies feature design and implementation; gz-skills supplies
portable engineering disciplines. Superpowers Backplane remains pinned for
future adoption but is disabled by default because readiness is incomplete.
Use existing project backlog and handoff practices in the meantime.

Project AGENTS.md, domain authorities and verification commands remain binding.
Keep project-owned operational skills, supporting domain code, and records
separate. Confirm actual discovery before invoking upstream entry skills;
configuration does not prove loading. Preserve independently versioned upstream
sources and avoid duplicate plugin/copied-skill discovery.

No lite/heavy profile or gzkit lifecycle is selected by the starter. For adoption,
structural backporting, updates and verification, use the reviewed starter at
https://github.com/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter. Existing project instructions
and app architecture are preserved until specific changes are authorized.

For projects adopting the starter's Python baseline, use the latest stable
release within each explicitly selected Python/tool release family. Python's
family is 3.14.x: verify the latest patch from official sources at setup/adoption
and scoped maintenance, then pin that exact patch for local execution and CI.
An already-installed version or a `3.14` selector does not prove freshness.
Keep tools pinned/locked after verification; changing families requires separate
review. Record any compatibility exception with evidence and a revisit condition,
including the documented XPPython3 host exception. Preserve project dependencies
and authorities, report adoption gaps, and follow the reviewed starter's Python
engineering skill. This rule does not authorize automatic upgrades or schedules.

At adoption and scoped maintenance, check this starter template, Superpowers,
Superpowers Backplane and gz-skills independently for upstream updates. Compare
the recorded starter/component SHAs with official published releases; where no
release exists, distinguish a reviewed published commit from a stable release.
Record the checked date, selected/latest versions or SHAs, compatibility evidence
and adopt/defer decisions. Review configuration changes before using native
update operations, preserve project additions and overrides, keep rollback pins,
and verify actual loaded sources in a fresh session. Track SP-BP freshness while
it is deferred; keep it disabled until readiness and explicit adoption are
established. Use the reviewed starter's `docs/adoption.md` maintenance procedure.

Generic maintenance belongs in gz-skills: use its discovered
`gzs-update-dependencies` for authorized dependency/tool updates and
`gzs-dependency-risk-audit` for risk assessments. The starter supplies baseline
policy and stack-specific binding guidance. Do not create a duplicate local
maintenance skill or generic freshness reporter. Freshness-only reporting and
expanded template/plugin inventory are upstream proposals; verify release support
before claiming those capabilities exist.

Track the adopted starter's own version and exact SHA in its bundle lock,
independently of app and upstream plugin versions. Compare reviewed template
releases and their changelog using the starter's `docs/versioning.md` policy.
A version label is not publication or readiness proof. Reconcile older
unversioned records without inventing historical provenance or overwriting
project changes.
releases.front_door_skill_template:
---
name: skills-first-start
description: Orient an agent in a skills-first project, choose among project workflows, Superpowers and gz-skills, or guide adoption and structural backporting of the starter.
---

# Start a skills-first task

Read the project's AGENTS.md and referenced authorities first. Identify the user's
actual task and available skills; recommend the smallest useful workflow and then
continue the authorized task. This skill is orientation, not another lifecycle.
Do not invoke every audit or reinterpret a small task as an architecture project.

For application operations, follow the project's own operational skills. For
engineering skill selection, prefer the discovered gz-skills `gzs-router` and
its maintained catalog; do not recreate that catalog here. For feature design
and implementation, use the installed SP `using-superpowers` entry and its
workflow. For adoption or structural backporting, read the starter's
`adopt-skills-stack` skill and `docs/backport.md` from a reviewed checkout.
For Python engineering, read `skills/python-engineering/SKILL.md` from the
reviewed starter checkout; it binds the runtime, idioms, routine tools and
on-demand hygiene selections. This path is not relative to the copied adopter
front door. Do not claim native discovery of that skill without evidence.
Backlog and handoff continuity stay with existing project practice while SP-BP,
an expected addition to the target stack, is deferred.

This is a bootstrap pointer. Broader cross-stack routing in `gzs-router` is a
future upstream integration; do not claim that the pinned router orchestrates
SP or starter adoption. Once that routing is shipped and verified, simplify
this pointer further rather than maintaining a parallel engineering catalog.

Check actual skill discovery before claiming an entry is available. A pinned
catalog or configuration is not an installed skill. If the target skill is
missing, identify the gap and use its reviewed source instructions when useful;
do not silently install it. The starter's own adoption skill can be read from a
reviewed checkout when it is not exposed through native discovery.

The maintained guidance lives at https://github.com/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter.
Use the revision recorded in `.skills-first/bundle.lock.json` when present.
From that reviewed checkout, `uv run --python 3.14.8 starter.py backport --project <root>` gives
a read-only starting assessment. Build a source-to-target mapping before changes;
retain project authorities, domain rules, records, and working verification.

SP and gz-skills are the current default pair. SP-BP stays cataloged but disabled
until readiness and explicit adoption are established. Do not invent its missing
issue automation or replace project backlog authority with local starter code.
No gz-skills lite/heavy profile is inferred here. Upstream main proposals are
not capabilities in the pinned release. Keep upstream sources independently
versioned, and never install their skills through duplicate discovery paths.

For current SP/gz-skills releases or development snapshots, follow the reviewed
starter's `docs/adoption.md` update procedure. Query upstream before saying
“latest”; preserve exact source pins and verify actual loading after an update.
The same maintenance review includes the starter template itself and deferred
SP-BP. Check all four independently at adoption and scoped maintenance; record
dates, upstream evidence and adopt/defer decisions. A newer SP-BP revision does
not authorize enabling it. Preserve project additions, overrides and rollback
pins when reconciling changes from a newer reviewed starter.

Route authorized dependency/tool updates to gz-skills `gzs-update-dependencies`
and dependency-risk assessments to `gzs-dependency-risk-audit`. The starter's
Python skill supplies policy, not a parallel generic maintenance workflow.
Freshness-only reporting and expanded template/plugin inventory remain upstream
enhancement proposals; do not invent a local skill or claim they have shipped.

releases.update_skill_template:
---
name: update-gz-template
description: Check or update a project's adopted gz-skills-first-starter template, explain released policy changes, and reconcile migration guidance. Use for starter-version reviews and template upgrades, rather than general package or plugin updates.
---

# Update the GZ template

Help an existing adopter consume released template policy without replacing its
product. The canonical repository is
`https://github.com/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter`. This is a narrow guide
to its maintained adoption instructions, not another dependency updater.

## Establish the request and current adoption

Read the target project's AGENTS and existing authorities. Confirm its root and
dirty state; preserve unrelated work. Read `.skills-first/bundle.lock.json` for
the starter repository, version/full SHA and independent component selections.
Read `.gz-skills/settings.json` for the explicit lite/heavy choice. Absent or
legacy provenance stays unknown; do not infer it from today's version label.

A request to check or explain updates authorizes review only. Do not sync,
resolve, install or modify the adopter in review mode. A request to upgrade
authorizes the scoped template reconciliation and necessary verification; use
that authorization without asking again for routine migration steps. Keep
runtime/tool/plugin refreshes separate unless required by the reviewed target
policy or included in the user's request. With no adoption record, identify
first adoption and follow the starter's greenfield/brownfield entry instead of
pretending this is an upgrade. A gzkit project retains its separate ecosystem.

## Find the released target and its instructions

Query the canonical repository's live stable releases through a connected
GitHub tool or GitHub CLI. For example:

```bash
gh api repos/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter/releases/latest --jq '{tag_name,html_url,published_at}'
```

Respect an explicitly requested published target. A failed query is UNKNOWN,
not proof of no updates. Distinguish a release from newer main; a version string
alone proves neither source identity nor publication. Use a separate clean
checkout of the selected tag, resolve `TAG^{commit}` to its full SHA, and compare
with HEAD and the target manifest before applying. Never use the adopter's own
HEAD as starter provenance.

Read the selected release notes, intervening changelogs, `docs/versioning.md`,
`docs/baseline-policy.md` and `docs/adoption-workflow.md` at that exact target.
Follow the current runbook linked there; do not freeze a historical filename or
copy its whole procedure into this skill. Release 0.5.0 links
`docs/adoption-0.5.md`; future releases may link a successor. If a tool cannot
fetch the required instructions, report that gap rather than guess the migration.
When present at the target, `docs/updating.md` owns the canonical update and
older-adopter bootstrap method. Reconcile this project skill along with the
other managed content; adding it alone does not upgrade the adopted baseline.

Compare policy changes as well as pins. Explain what applies to this product,
what needs reconciliation and what is deferred. If `gzs-update-dependencies`
is actually discovered, compose its template-inventory/review or scoped-update
mode under project policy. Its absence does not prevent reading the release and
following the published runbook; do not claim an undiscovered skill ran.

## Reconcile an authorized upgrade

Follow the target's brownfield-upgrade path. Capture rollback; compare the
original starter-managed content, current project edits and target candidates.
Generate candidates in a disposable directory using the clean target checkout.
Review the actual diff before changing product files. The helper intentionally
refuses different existing records; no force-overwrite or delete-and-reconfigure
shortcut is supplied.

Reconcile the instructions fragment, project policy references, starter
version/full SHA and managed host tables together. Preserve application
dependencies/settings, public behavior, explicit lane and local guidance.
Do not overwrite existing AGENTS with a generated example or hand-edit uv.lock.
Leave native caches to their manager; a template change does not automatically
authorize plugin activation. Backplane remains subject to its readiness rule.

Execute the target's applicable migration, analysis and artifact checks. Keep
lane, configuration, Python acceptance and native discovery as separate results.
Missing/null lane, required failed/unknown/stale evidence or accepted exceptions
cannot become an unqualified strict-conformance claim. Mark unfinished work as
migration pending. Do not alter the product version or manufacture a major PRD
merely because the independent template version changed.

## Report

Give the checked date; old and target starter versions/full SHAs; release link;
policy delta; adopt/defer decision; changed files; observed checks and remaining
migration/readiness gaps; and rollback reference. A review must clearly state
that no update was applied. An applied upgrade must distinguish updated
configuration from completed conformance. Never call the whole stack current
based only on the template. Do not publish releases or notify other adopters
unless the user separately requests those actions.

# Update the GZ template

Help an existing adopter consume released template policy without replacing its
product. The canonical repository is
`https://github.com/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter`. This is a narrow guide
to its maintained adoption instructions, not another dependency updater.

## Establish the request and current adoption

Read the target project's AGENTS and existing authorities. Confirm its root and
dirty state; preserve unrelated work. Read `.skills-first/bundle.lock.json` for
the starter repository, version/full SHA and independent component selections.
Read `.gz-skills/settings.json` for the explicit lite/heavy choice. Absent or
legacy provenance stays unknown; do not infer it from today's version label.

A request to check or explain updates authorizes review only. Do not sync,
resolve, install or modify the adopter in review mode. A request to upgrade
authorizes the scoped template reconciliation and necessary verification; use
that authorization without asking again for routine migration steps. Keep
runtime/tool/plugin refreshes separate unless required by the reviewed target
policy or included in the user's request. With no adoption record, identify
first adoption and follow the starter's greenfield/brownfield entry instead of
pretending this is an upgrade. A gzkit project retains its separate ecosystem.

## Find the released target and its instructions

Query the canonical repository's live stable releases through a connected
GitHub tool or GitHub CLI. For example:

```bash
gh api repos/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter/releases/latest --jq '{tag_name,html_url,published_at}'
```

Respect an explicitly requested published target. A failed query is UNKNOWN,
not proof of no updates. Distinguish a release from newer main; a version string
alone proves neither source identity nor publication. Use a separate clean
checkout of the selected tag, resolve `TAG^{commit}` to its full SHA, and compare
with HEAD and the target manifest before applying. Never use the adopter's own
HEAD as starter provenance.

Read the selected release notes, intervening changelogs, `docs/versioning.md`,
`docs/baseline-policy.md` and `docs/adoption-workflow.md` at that exact target.
Follow the current runbook linked there; do not freeze a historical filename or
copy its whole procedure into this skill. Release 0.5.0 links
`docs/adoption-0.5.md`; future releases may link a successor. If a tool cannot
fetch the required instructions, report that gap rather than guess the migration.
When present at the target, `docs/updating.md` owns the canonical update and
older-adopter bootstrap method. Reconcile this project skill along with the
other managed content; adding it alone does not upgrade the adopted baseline.

Compare policy changes as well as pins. Enforce the target's latest-tooling
requirement: an old allowed tool family is not proof of currency. Required stale
or unknown freshness blocks strict acceptance; record any explicit owned
compatibility exception as conditional/noncurrent. The adopter retains this
responsibility when composing an upstream maintenance skill. Explain what applies to this product,
what needs reconciliation and what is deferred. If `gzs-update-dependencies`
is actually discovered, compose its template-inventory/review or scoped-update
mode under project policy. Its absence does not prevent reading the release and
following the published runbook; do not claim an undiscovered skill ran.

## Reconcile an authorized upgrade

Follow the target's brownfield-upgrade path. Capture rollback; compare the
original starter-managed content, current project edits and target candidates.
Generate candidates in a disposable directory using the clean target checkout.
Review the actual diff before changing product files. The helper intentionally
refuses different existing records; no force-overwrite or delete-and-reconfigure
shortcut is supplied.

Reconcile the instructions fragment, project policy references, starter
version/full SHA and managed host tables together. Preserve application
dependencies/settings, public behavior, explicit lane and local guidance.
Do not overwrite existing AGENTS with a generated example or hand-edit uv.lock.
Leave native caches to their manager; a template change does not automatically
authorize plugin activation. Backplane remains subject to its readiness rule.

Execute the target's applicable migration, analysis and artifact checks. Keep
lane, configuration, Python acceptance and native discovery as separate results.
Missing/null lane, required failed/unknown/stale evidence or accepted exceptions
cannot become an unqualified strict-conformance claim. Mark unfinished work as
migration pending. Do not alter the product version or manufacture a major PRD
merely because the independent template version changed.

## Report

Give the checked date; old and target starter versions/full SHAs; release link;
policy delta; adopt/defer decision; changed files; observed checks and remaining
migration/readiness gaps; and rollback reference. A review must clearly state
that no update was applied. An applied upgrade must distinguish updated
configuration from completed conformance. Never call the whole stack current
based only on the template. Do not publish releases or notify other adopters
unless the user separately requests those actions.

---
name: update-gz-template
description: Check or update a project's adopted gz-skills-first-starter template, explain released policy changes, and reconcile migration guidance. Use for starter-version reviews and template upgrades, rather than general package or plugin updates.
---

# Update the GZ template

Help an existing adopter consume released template policy without replacing its
product. The canonical repository is
`https://github.com/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter`. This is a narrow guide
to its maintained adoption instructions, not another dependency updater.

## Establish the request and current adoption

Read the target project's AGENTS and existing authorities. Confirm its root and
dirty state; preserve unrelated work. Read `.skills-first/bundle.lock.json` for
the starter repository, version/full SHA and independent component selections.
Read `.gz-skills/settings.json` for the explicit lite/heavy choice. Absent or
legacy provenance stays unknown; do not infer it from today's version label.
Read the lock's selected native `host`; legacy records without it use Codex.
Use that host's repository-owned settings. For activation-only repair, follow
the reviewed starter's `localize --host` procedure; do not rewrite adoption
provenance or uninstall existing global copies. Installation, version updates
and enablement MUST remain separate. Project commands MUST preserve local scope.

A request to check or explain updates authorizes review only. Do not sync,
resolve, install or modify the adopter in review mode. A request to upgrade
authorizes the scoped template reconciliation and necessary verification; use
that authorization without asking again for routine migration steps. Keep
runtime/tool/plugin refreshes separate unless required by the reviewed target
policy or included in the user's request. With no adoption record, identify
first adoption and follow the starter's greenfield/brownfield entry instead of
pretending this is an upgrade. A gzkit project retains its separate ecosystem.

## Find the released target and its instructions

Query the canonical repository's live stable releases with direct `gh` commands.
Use direct `git` commands for repository operations. Do not wrap routine CLI
calls in Python; substantive Python processing must use the prescribed locked,
uv-managed environment. For example:

```bash
gh api repos/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter/releases/latest --jq '{tag_name,html_url,published_at}'
```

Respect an explicitly requested published target. A failed query is UNKNOWN,
not proof of no updates. Distinguish a release from newer main; a version string
alone proves neither source identity nor publication. Use a separate clean
checkout of the selected tag, resolve `TAG^{commit}` to its full SHA, and compare
with HEAD and the target manifest before applying. Never use the adopter's own
HEAD as starter provenance.

Read the selected release notes, intervening changelogs, `docs/versioning.md`,
`docs/baseline-policy.md` and `docs/adoption-workflow.md` at that exact target.
Follow the current runbook linked there; do not freeze a historical filename or
copy its whole procedure into this skill. Release 0.5.0 links
`docs/adoption-0.5.md`; future releases may link a successor. If a tool cannot
fetch the required instructions, report that gap rather than guess the migration.
When present at the target, `docs/updating.md` owns the canonical update and
older-adopter bootstrap method. Reconcile this project skill along with the
other managed content; adding it alone does not upgrade the adopted baseline.

Compare policy changes as well as pins. Enforce the target's latest-tooling
requirement: an old allowed tool family is not proof of currency. Required stale
or unknown freshness blocks strict acceptance; record any explicit owned
compatibility exception as conditional/noncurrent. The adopter retains this
responsibility when composing an upstream maintenance skill. Explain what applies to this product,
what needs reconciliation and what is deferred. If `gzs-update-dependencies`
is actually discovered, compose its template-inventory/review or scoped-update
mode under project policy. Its absence does not prevent reading the release and
following the published runbook; do not claim an undiscovered skill ran.

## Reconcile an authorized upgrade

Follow the target's brownfield-upgrade path. Capture rollback; compare the
original starter-managed content, current project edits and target candidates.
Generate candidates in a disposable directory using the clean target checkout.
Review the actual diff before changing product files. The helper intentionally
refuses different existing records; no force-overwrite or delete-and-reconfigure
shortcut is supplied.

Reconcile the instructions fragment, project policy references, starter
version/full SHA and managed host tables together. Preserve application
dependencies/settings, public behavior, explicit lane and local guidance.
Do not overwrite existing AGENTS with a generated example or hand-edit uv.lock.
Leave native caches to their manager; a template change does not automatically
authorize plugin activation. Backplane remains subject to its readiness rule.

Execute the target's applicable migration, analysis and artifact checks. Keep
lane, configuration, Python acceptance and native discovery as separate results.
Missing/null lane, required failed/unknown/stale evidence or accepted exceptions
cannot become an unqualified strict-conformance claim. Mark unfinished work as
migration pending. Do not alter the product version or manufacture a major PRD
merely because the independent template version changed.

## Report

Give the checked date; old and target starter versions/full SHAs; release link;
policy delta; adopt/defer decision; changed files; observed checks and remaining
migration/readiness gaps; and rollback reference. A review must clearly state
that no update was applied. An applied upgrade must distinguish updated
configuration from completed conformance. Never call the whole stack current
based only on the template. Do not publish releases or notify other adopters
unless the user separately requests those actions.

Require the latest stable baseline tools across tool families. Review new stable
families and verify compatibility; an old range or exact pin is not a freshness
exemption. Required stale/unknown freshness blocks adoption and release acceptance.
The adopter owns that decision even when gz-skills performs the review. Retained
older tools need an explicit evidenced exception, owner and dated revisit and
remain conditional/noncurrent. Check official releases at setup/adoption, before
each release and scoped maintenance; pin package selections and record the tested
uv version separately from its minimum compatibility requirement. Python's
family follows the user-directed N-1 rule: one stable minor behind, currently
3.14.x for ordinary projects. XPPython3-bound code retains its supported 3.12.x
host exception. This runtime policy does not exempt old tool families. Verify the latest
stable host-compatible patch from official sources at setup/adoption
and scoped maintenance, then pin that exact patch for local execution and CI.
An already-installed version or a `3.14` selector does not prove freshness.
The starter's current exact patch is a reproducibility baseline, not a permanent
adopter requirement. XPPython3 controls its embedded interpreter; inspect and test
that runtime separately, recording host limitations and revisit conditions.
Keep tools pinned/locked after verification; changing families requires separate
review. Record any compatibility exception with evidence and a revisit condition,
including the documented XPPython3 host exception. Preserve project dependencies
and authorities, report adoption gaps, and follow the reviewed starter's Python
engineering policy at `docs/engineering/python.md` in the reviewed starter
checkout. Keep Ruff check/format, ty and unittest (never pytest) as routine checks
through uv and pre-commit; execute applicable deeper analysis at adoption and
release acceptance, plus on demand, outside routine hooks and routine CI.
Retain evidence and reviewed findings; required FAIL/UNKNOWN/stale results block
strict acceptance. Accepted exceptions are conditional, never 100% conformance.
Report missing
tool installation or enforcement as a gap. Adopters choose starter updates,
independent upstream updates or both, and own update timing and verification.
The starter permits scheduled scans and reviewed update PRs covering standard
and X-Plane/XPPython3 baselines separately; see
`docs/baseline-policy.md#scheduled-dependency-scanning` in the reviewed starter
checkout. No adopter scanning service or schedule is imposed. Automatic merge,
release publication and native plugin installation require separate authority.

The reviewed Python policy's on-demand tools form the adopter minimum standard,
independent of the starter helper's needs. Include project-pinned `cohesion` for
class cohesion analysis; verify its standalone CLI on the selected runtime and
representative invented classes. Record scopes, scores and reviewed findings;
record not-applicable scopes with reasons and report missing installation or
compatibility evidence as gaps. Preserve project-specific thresholds and keep
cohesion outside routine hooks and routine CI. Complexipy is under qualification
review: known keyword-conditional under-counting means a clean score alone cannot
pass cognitive acceptance. Read the current qualification evidence before relying
on that analyzer. The selected replacement direction is gzkit's CPython AST
scoring approach, preferably through one shared package; qualification and
distribution must be verified before claiming it is installed or authoritative.
See the reviewed starter's
`docs/engineering/python.md` for the full selected tool set and interpretation.

Keep code current with its selected Python family, not just its interpreter pin.
gz-skills owns runtime discovery; require its workflows to honor this project's
adopted version-range and engineering policy, report missing/conflicting evidence
and validate host-bound behavior separately. This template supplies policy, not
an upstream discovery procedure.
gz-skills supplies no competing family/tool/package standard for this project.
Read the recorded adopted authority; if it is unavailable, keep dependent
decisions unresolved instead of treating a stored pin or workflow default as policy.
At adoption, runtime-family changes, feature design, code review and scoped
maintenance, assess relevant idioms, stdlib advances and deprecations using
versioned official documentation. Record benefits, risks and adopt/defer decisions;
apply useful changes within authorized scope. Use SP and gz-skills workflows with
the reviewed starter's `docs/engineering/python.md` and version opportunity guide.
XPPython3-bound code must stay within 3.12/host capabilities. The pinned gz-skills
Pythonic-pattern skills cover pattern simplification and `gzs-cross-platform-python`
covers OS seams. Read `docs/gz-skills-python.md` in the reviewed starter for the
verified mapping; those workflows do not establish a complete version audit.
Report missing workflow coverage rather than inventing a starter skill or claiming
that a current runtime proves current code.

At setup/adoption, before each release, scoped upgrades and quarterly on-demand
maintenance, check this starter template, Superpowers,
Superpowers Backplane and gz-skills independently for upstream updates. Compare
the recorded starter/component SHAs with official published releases; where no
release exists, distinguish a reviewed published commit from a stable release.
Review template changelogs for baseline-policy changes as well as dependency
versions; a new template release does not automatically change project policy.
Record the checked date, selected/latest versions or SHAs, compatibility evidence
and adopt/defer decisions. Review configuration changes before using native
update operations, preserve project additions and overrides, keep rollback pins,
and verify actual loaded sources in a fresh session. Track SP-BP freshness while
it is deferred; keep it disabled until readiness and explicit adoption are
established. Use the reviewed starter's `docs/adoption.md` maintenance procedure.

Generic maintenance belongs in gz-skills: use its discovered
`gzs-update-dependencies` for authorized dependency/tool updates and
`gzs-dependency-risk-audit` for risk assessments. The starter supplies baseline
policy and stack-specific binding guidance. Do not create a duplicate local
maintenance skill or generic freshness reporter. The pinned gz-skills v0.8.3
supplies freshness-only review and template/plugin inventory. Review mode leaves
pins and environments unchanged; preserve project policy and profile choices.
End a freshness review with a concrete recommended upgrade batch and an explicit
offer to apply it. Strongly recommend supported updates that satisfy project
policy; state targets, benefits, compatibility risks and required checks. Do not
stop at an inventory or adopt/defer table. If updates are already authorized,
perform and verify them without asking again. State evidenced deferrals; if
everything is current, say so instead of inventing an upgrade.

Track the adopted starter's own version and exact SHA in its bundle lock,
independently of app and upstream plugin versions. Compare reviewed template
releases and their changelog using the starter's `docs/versioning.md` policy.
A version label is not publication or readiness proof. Reconcile older
unversioned records without inventing historical provenance or overwriting
project changes.
releases.update_skill_template:
---
name: update-gz-template
description: Check or update a project's adopted gz-skills-first-starter template, explain released policy changes, and reconcile migration guidance. Use for starter-version reviews and template upgrades, rather than general package or plugin updates.
---

# Update the GZ template

Help an existing adopter consume released template policy without replacing its
product. The canonical repository is
`https://github.com/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter`. This is a narrow guide
to its maintained adoption instructions, not another dependency updater.

## Establish the request and current adoption

Read the target project's AGENTS and existing authorities. Confirm its root and
dirty state; preserve unrelated work. Read `.skills-first/bundle.lock.json` for
the starter repository, version/full SHA and independent component selections.
Read `.gz-skills/settings.json` for the explicit lite/heavy choice. Absent or
legacy provenance stays unknown; do not infer it from today's version label.
Read the lock's selected native `host`; legacy records without it use Codex.
Use that host's repository-owned settings. For activation-only repair, follow
the reviewed starter's `localize --host` procedure; do not rewrite adoption
provenance or uninstall existing global copies. Installation, version updates
and enablement MUST remain separate. Project commands MUST preserve local scope.

A request to check or explain updates authorizes review only. Do not sync,
resolve, install or modify the adopter in review mode. A request to upgrade
authorizes the scoped template reconciliation and necessary verification; use
that authorization without asking again for routine migration steps. Keep
runtime/tool/plugin refreshes separate unless required by the reviewed target
policy or included in the user's request. With no adoption record, identify
first adoption and follow the starter's greenfield/brownfield entry instead of
pretending this is an upgrade. A gzkit project retains its separate ecosystem.

## Find the released target and its instructions

Query the canonical repository's live stable releases with direct `gh` commands.
Use direct `git` commands for repository operations. Do not wrap routine CLI
calls in Python; substantive Python processing must use the prescribed locked,
uv-managed environment. For example:

```bash
gh api repos/tvproductions/gz-skills-first-starter/releases/latest --jq '{tag_name,html_url,published_at}'
```

Respect an explicitly requested published target. A failed query is UNKNOWN,
not proof of no updates. Distinguish a release from newer main; a version string
alone proves neither source identity nor publication. Use a separate clean
checkout of the selected tag, resolve `TAG^{commit}` to its full SHA, and compare
with HEAD and the target manifest before applying. Never use the adopter's own
HEAD as starter provenance.

Read the selected release notes, intervening changelogs, `docs/versioning.md`,
`docs/baseline-policy.md` and `docs/adoption-workflow.md` at that exact target.
Follow the current runbook linked there; do not freeze a historical filename or
copy its whole procedure into this skill. Release 0.5.0 links
`docs/adoption-0.5.md`; future releases may link a successor. If a tool cannot
fetch the required instructions, report that gap rather than guess the migration.
When present at the target, `docs/updating.md` owns the canonical update and
older-adopter bootstrap method. Reconcile this project skill along with the
other managed content; adding it alone does not upgrade the adopted baseline.

Compare policy changes as well as pins. Enforce the target's latest-tooling
requirement: an old allowed tool family is not proof of currency. Required stale
or unknown freshness blocks strict acceptance; record any explicit owned
compatibility exception as conditional/noncurrent. The adopter retains this
responsibility when composing an upstream maintenance skill. Explain what applies to this product,
what needs reconciliation and what is deferred. If `gzs-update-dependencies`
is actually discovered, compose its template-inventory/review or scoped-update
mode under project policy. Its absence does not prevent reading the release and
following the published runbook; do not claim an undiscovered skill ran.

## Reconcile an authorized upgrade

Follow the target's brownfield-upgrade path. Capture rollback; compare the
original starter-managed content, current project edits and target candidates.
Generate candidates in a disposable directory using the clean target checkout.
Review the actual diff before changing product files. The helper intentionally
refuses different existing records; no force-overwrite or delete-and-reconfigure
shortcut is supplied.

Reconcile the instructions fragment, project policy references, starter
version/full SHA and managed host tables together. Preserve application
dependencies/settings, public behavior, explicit lane and local guidance.
Do not overwrite existing AGENTS with a generated example or hand-edit uv.lock.
Leave native caches to their manager; a template change does not automatically
authorize plugin activation. Backplane remains subject to its readiness rule.

Execute the target's applicable migration, analysis and artifact checks. Keep
lane, configuration, Python acceptance and native discovery as separate results.
Missing/null lane, required failed/unknown/stale evidence or accepted exceptions
cannot become an unqualified strict-conformance claim. Mark unfinished work as
migration pending. Do not alter the product version or manufacture a major PRD
merely because the independent template version changed.

## Report

Give the checked date; old and target starter versions/full SHAs; release link;
policy delta; adopt/defer decision; changed files; observed checks and remaining
migration/readiness gaps; and rollback reference. A review must clearly state
that no update was applied. An applied upgrade must distinguish updated
configuration from completed conformance. Never call the whole stack current
based only on the template. Do not publish releases or notify other adopters
unless the user separately requests those actions.

releases.adr_policy_template:
# Architectural decision policy

This starter policy applies to both lite and heavy adopters and to the starter's
own development. Use the project's existing authorities and suitable ADR
conventions. The starter owns this mandatory binding; gz-skills owns the portable
procedure/template, SP owns feature workflows and Backplane owns its existing
planning/tracking integration. Adopt no GZKit ledger or lifecycle through it.

Source: the [operator-accepted lightweight guidance and sample](https://github.com/wtcis-pvecob/cob_projects/blob/dd1ab883c04e884678ed723959b17c5c364263d1/docs/engineering/proposals/2026-11-07-gz-adr-workflow-discussion.md#final-audience-guidance),
as bound by the approved starter design. Starter distribution follows ADR-0001
(`docs/decisions/ADR-0001-001-qualify-exact-component-combinations.md` in the
canonical starter source identified by the recorded revision):
qualify exact reviewed component combinations; keep independent versions/releases.

## Recognize, reuse and align

During design, implementation and review, inspect applicable decisions and
accepted constraints before introducing consequential choices about ownership,
dependencies, interfaces, persistence, recovery, trust, deployment or operation.
Reuse applicable approved decisions and cite them; do not demand another ADR or
approval for routine work within their scope.

For a new, conflicting or materially replacement choice, explain the choice,
credible alternatives, consequences and material uncertainty. Draft the ADR and
obtain separate explicit human approval of its identified edition before
dependent implementation. A design, plan, green test or release approval does
not substitute. Pause only dependent work, including for choices discovered
mid-implementation; continue independent authorized work. Surface conflicting
authorities rather than selecting an undocumented winner.

Recover existing justification first. Investigate important gaps proportionately;
require neither a new research artifact nor external precedent for every ADR.
Code shows what exists, not necessarily why it was chosen or approved. Disclose
inference and unknown history. Correct implementation drift against an approved
choice; do not rewrite the choice to bless conflicting code.

## Keep the decision and its approval together

Keep the choice, scope, context, credible alternatives, rationale, consequences,
approval metadata and amendment history in the ADR. Include a Confirmation
approach when useful; keep test output, progress and delivery claims in existing
verification/planning records. An optional index only helps locate decisions.

For a new collection, use `ADR-0001-001-title-in-kebab-case.md`: stable unique
decision identity, positive integer edition and descriptive title. Never reuse
an id. Preserve suitable existing conventions through an explicit semantic
mapping, not blanket renaming. The starter's own collection is `docs/decisions/`.
Project instructions must identify the project's actual collection.

Authoritative records use Current or Retired and carry `id`, `title`, `revision`,
`state`, `decision_date`, `revision_date`, `approved_by`, `approved_revision` and
`approval_ref`. Use actual YYYY-MM-DD dates and the authorized human's project
identity. Drafts confer no authority; do not fill approval fields with invented
values or mark an unapproved record Current.

Approval evidence must preserve the actual explicit approval of the identified
edition and its reviewed content. Use a retrievable conversation/review reference
and immutable content reference, or preserve the actual interaction with its
source context, date, identity and exact reviewed bytes/hash. Evidence may be
embedded in the ADR or durably referenced from it; no separate receipt file is
mandatory. Label an agent transcription honestly. A hash/commit identifies
content, while only the actual human response establishes approval. Preserve
the proposal before administrative approval capture and disclose that transition.

## Preserve history and independent evolution

Keep earlier editions retrievable by version history or an existing preserved-
document mechanism. Keep the latest filename as the working ADR and repair
affected links after renames. Approval references retain the reviewed edition.

For editorial changes that preserve the choice, scope and constraints, increment
the edition, update its date/filename and record the previous edition, edit,
editor and existing review/change reference. Preserve the original decision
date and approved revision. Use ordinary documentation review; no architectural
reapproval or additional reviewer is required for a typo. Surface uncertain
meaning rather than calling it editorial. A materially changed choice receives
a new, separately approved ADR.

Retirement requires explicit authority, date, reason and a replacement reference
where applicable. Preserve the record and approval history. Do not disguise
retirement as an editorial amendment. Backfill honestly: distinguish documented
approval, observed code, inferred rationale and unknowns. Disclose unsupported
historical dates as unknown; obtain missing approval now without backdating it.
No blanket historical backfill is required by this binding.

Decisions, requirements, features, designs/plans, evidence, instructions and
releases evolve independently. Links express applicability and constraints,
not one-to-one containment, matching versions or automatic revision cascades.
Recheck affected relationships after changes; amend a record only when its own
meaning/applicability changes. ADR approval adds no data, migration, deployment
or publication permission. Preserve and use existing authority without redundant
requests.

## Access, workflow availability and qualification

Project instructions may identify an immutable source link, a repository-local
policy copy, or both. Record starter version/full SHA, source path and original
content hash for local copies; preserve and review project adaptations. When a
local copy is selected, use it as the identified working policy and retain the
canonical link for comparison. Surface applicable local/source conflicts;
do not silently switch sources or overwrite project changes. If required policy,
procedure or approval content is unreadable, report the gap and withhold affected
completion claims while continuing independent authorized work.

Consult the exact selected gz-skills portable procedure/template when its owning
delivery is verified. Released gz-skills 0.13.0 supplies
`gzs-architectural-decisions` and its template; the source-bound qualification
receipt is `docs/evidence/2026-11-15-adr-combination.md` in the starter. Verify
actual installed/discovered sources before extending its observed scope. Heavy mode uses existing supported
Backplane records; no new approval ledger/service is introduced. When Backplane
is disabled, retain existing planning/review/handoff tools in either lane.

Before adopter propagation, require immutable released companion contributions,
full shared behavioral evaluation plus targeted binding checks (including both
missing-approval stopping and approved-decision continuation), and genuine
internal use/alignment review in all three publishers. Expand affected evaluation
when bindings change shared behavior or expose discrepancies. Record exact
sources, loaded configuration, actual observations and limitations in existing
release evidence. Configuration, metadata and passing helper tests alone prove
none of behavioral compliance, native discovery or approval.
