releases.fragment_template:
# Skills-first development stack

Read the project's `AGENTS.md` and linked authorities first. Preserve its
domain rules, decisions, verification commands and app architecture. These
starter requirements are mandatory. Execute the owning workflow and checks,
record evidence, and report unmet requirements and policy-approved exceptions.
Preserve failing results. Verify installed revisions and discovery separately
from configuration.

**Resolve starter references from the source, version and exact SHA in
`.skills-first/bundle.lock.json`.** Read the named `docs/` sections in that
reviewed starter checkout, or use a project-owned reconciliation with recorded
provenance. If the governing source is unavailable, report the gap and leave
dependent decisions unresolved. Recognize **GZ Starter**, **starter** and
**starter template** as shorthand for `gz-starter`. Preserve canonical IDs in
commands and provenance. Route “update the starter” or “check the starter
template” through `update-gz-template` or `docs/updating.md` in the corresponding
update or review mode. Clarify only if the reference is ambiguous.

**Dependency maintenance MUST complete migration to the latest stable versions
of every in-scope dependency and tool, including new families.** Bare
`gzs-update-dependencies` is update mode. Review-only requires an explicit check,
assessment or no-changes request. Preserve the approved Python families,
product contracts, thresholds and evidenced exceptions in
`docs/baseline-policy.md#dependency-maintenance-means-completed-migration`.
At session start, do one bounded freshness check against official sources using
applicable recent dated evidence, flag stale or unavailable results, and migrate
only in separately authorized maintenance. Follow
`docs/engineering/verification-policy.md#session-start-freshness-is-a-check`.

## Work and verify

**Starter is the outer loop, SP is the inner loop, and gz-skills is supplemental.**
Starter frames objective, authorized scope, requirements and completion. Use
SP's `using-superpowers` for development within those boundaries, gz-skills
`gzs-router` for distinct supplemental engineering needs, and project-owned
skills for project operations. Confirm actual plugin discovery before invoking
upstream workflows. Read
`docs/architecture.md#outer-loop-inner-loop-and-supplemental-disciplines`.
The starter owns only `update-gz-template`, its helper, configuration, provenance
and policy. Keep generic workflows and skills upstream.

Use direct `git` and `gh` commands. Use Python for substantive processing through
`uv run --locked python`, honoring the exact managed pin and supported uv.
Follow SP verification-before-completion and
`docs/engineering/verification-policy.md`. Run each selected command in full,
freshly, for changed behavior and affected consumers. Keep full checks for
broad/uncertain changes, verification or dependency/workspace changes, and
integration/release checkpoints. Keep affected/focused hook checks and full
checks runnable. Add tests for meaningful defects at the owning seam. Review
diff and references for documentation-only changes and use relevant changed-file,
existing test and invented rendered checks for bounded presentation changes.
Cite dated, input-matched historical evidence as such. Repeat affected checks
when inputs or risk change and record scope and limits.

## Adoption, decisions and native scope

This starter supports Python only, in both lite and heavy lanes. At adoption,
select an explicit lane through the pinned gz-skills setup workflow. Missing
or null selection leaves adoption incomplete. Both lanes require the same
applicable Python baseline, SemVer, major-release PRDs and adoption/release
analysis. Follow `docs/adoption-0.5.md` for greenfield adoption, brownfield
first adoption, structural backport or upgrades. Backplane owns requirements tracking, labeling,
release/backlog monitoring, handoffs and lane definitions. Read
https://github.com/tvproductions/superpowers-backplane/blob/main/docs/superpowers-backplane/modes.md
when selecting a lane. Heavy targets SP, Backplane and gz-skills. Keep Backplane
disabled pending readiness and explicit adoption, report that gap, and preserve
existing planning and handoff authority without creating a ledger or gzkit
lifecycle.

During design, execution and review in either lane, follow the
[identified ADR policy]({{ADR_POLICY_WORKING_SOURCE}}). Preserve its
[immutable canonical source]({{ADR_POLICY_CANONICAL_URL}}) and the version, full
SHA, content hash and link/local choice in `.skills-first/bundle.lock.json`.
Honor the selected working copy, preserve local adaptations and report source
conflicts. Identify and retain the project's existing ADR collection and reuse
approved entries. Obtain separate explicit human approval of the exact new or
replacement edition before dependent implementation. Continue independent
authorized work. Keep approval evidence and edition history with the ADR.
General spec, plan, test or release approval does not approve an ADR. Use the
selected gz-skills `gzs-architectural-decisions` procedure only after verifying
its source and actual discovery. Follow `docs/adoption.md#architectural-decision-policy-access`
during ADR policy adoption or reconciliation.

Install and activate only at repository/project scope. Keep installation,
version updates and activation separate. Preserve user defaults and installs,
suppress inherited duplicates in project config, and report unsupported scope
without broadening activation. A shared cache grants no activation authority.
Before adoption, brownfield repair or updates, follow
`docs/adoption.md#repository-owned-installation-and-brownfield-repair` and
`docs/adoption.md#updates-and-rollback`. Preview, review and apply `localize` for
activation repair. Use `configure --host` for full adoption. Verify installed
revisions and enablement separately, including the outside-project control.
Codex CLI 0.166.0 `plugin add` enables user-wide. Do not use it for project
installation, updates or reinstalls. For OpenCode 2.2.0 project
commands, use the reviewed starter's `uv run --locked gz-starter run-opencode
--project <root> -- <native arguments>`. Read `docs/adoption.md#opencode` for its
scope and actual discovery checks.

## Python baseline and configuration

Use uv-managed Python N-1 (currently 3.14.x) and the 3.12.x XPPython3 host
exception. Verify the latest compatible patch in the approved family against
official sources at setup/adoption, release preparation and maintenance. Pin it
exactly in `.python-version` and CI. Test the embedded runtime separately.
Follow `docs/baseline-policy.md#allowed-python-families`. Keep uv compatibility
minimum-only, record CI's exact tested uv separately, and let supported callers
use their actual version with recorded provenance. Keep exact package/backend
locks and the Python pin independent of the uv executable floor. Follow
`docs/baseline-policy.md#uv-executable-compatibility`.

For Python work read `docs/engineering/python.md`. Meet
`docs/engineering/astral-alignment.md` and complete
`docs/engineering/astral-acceptance.md` at adoption and affected reconciliation,
using its worked migrations. Use `src/` packaging, uv_build for pure Python,
installed imports, entry points for apps and `py.typed` for typed libraries.
Centralize shared settings in root `pyproject.toml`, commit `uv.lock` and ignore
`.venv`. For multi-package work, apply
`docs/engineering/astral-alignment.md#workspaces` before changing workspace
structure. Use one root lock/environment and explicit member edges. Require an
explicit boundary for independent host/runtime environments. Reconcile
nonconforming layout and settings while preserving behavior, data and authorities.
Configuration-only work reports remaining refactoring. Verify effective
configuration, tool/runtime provenance, exact environments, and source-independent
builds and clean installed behavior. Record configuration, Python acceptance
and native discovery separately. Evidenced departures need an owner and revisit.

At adoption and when defining or changing a product's deployment or
configuration boundary, apply ADR-0002, `docs/project-configuration.md` and
`docs/engineering/application-foundations.md` in both lanes. Identify the
deployment unit, configuration owner/location, schema, selection/overrides,
permissions, upgrade preservation and any consuming application/host. Use
`settings.json` for operator-managed runtime settings, keep packaging/tool
settings in `pyproject.toml` and pass validated values to domain code. Reject
supplied or resolved paths containing spaces before reading content or writing.
Preserve data and settings during migration and verify actual consumer behavior.
For architectural warnings or naming/layout advice, read
`docs/engineering/application-foundations.md#warnings-and-informed-departures`
and `docs/engineering/naming-and-layout.md`. Record informed departures once,
preserving mandatory requirements and approved ADRs.

Keep routine hooks limited to locked Ruff check/format, ty and unittest through
pre-commit. Use `docs/engineering/verification-policy.md#bootstrap-and-implementation-verification-for-adopters`
for the fixed adopter hook and automatic first-source transition. Keep existing
coverage and workspace or embedded-host gates. Never use pytest. Run applicable deeper analyses, including C901,
at adoption, release acceptance and on demand outside routine hooks/CI. Follow
`docs/engineering/python.md#adoptionrelease-analysis-and-on-demand-hygiene` for
the adopter minimum and `docs/engineering/python.md#adopter-class-cohesion-requirement`
for project-owned cohesion pins, runtime proofs and reporting. A required
missing, failed or stale result blocks strict acceptance. Apply
`docs/engineering/cognitive-integration.md#starter-wide-qualification-deferral`.
Record **DEFERRED / measurement UNKNOWN**, retain ceiling 15 and all other checks,
and report conditional acceptance. Missing shared-engine delivery alone neither
blocks progress nor requires an adopter waiver. Revisit at release preparation
and candidate delivery. End the deferral only after independent qualification
and measurement for the actual consumer. Keep Complexipy for defect reproduction.

At adoption, Python-family changes, design, review and scoped maintenance, use
versioned official documentation and
`docs/engineering/python.md#version-aware-design` to assess idioms, stdlib changes
and deprecations. Record concrete benefits, risks and adopt/defer decisions.
For pattern and OS-seam work, use `docs/gz-skills-python.md` to find the selected
gz-skills workflows, including `gzs-cross-platform-python`. Preserve the bound
runtime policy, report missing or conflicting evidence, and verify the actual
host separately.

## Version and maintenance decisions

At requirements intake, planning and change closeout, execute
`docs/versioning.md#required-version-decision-procedure`. PRDs guide majors,
selected work and requirements drive minors, and compatible fixes drive patches.
Every major, including 1.0.0, requires a newly written PRD. Keep the existing
release-scope record and classify the complete pending scope. Derive routine
bumps, reuse a valid target and require a finite initial release. Keep metadata,
runtime, lock and changelog mirrors aligned. Missing required PRD, scope or
version evidence blocks the applicable claim. Report baseline → target,
governing work, compatibility, mirror agreement and publication state. Reserve
`0.0.0` for an unpublished bare scaffold. Set `0.1.0` as soon as original
implementation, tests, docs or configuration is added. Preserve published
versions and tags. Keep app, starter and upstream component versions independent.
Use `docs/versioning.md#classify-compatibility-within-the-selected-scope` for
increment rules and `docs/versioning.md#adopter-provenance-and-upgrades` when
reconciling an older lock or upgrading the starter. Use
`docs/versioning.md#ecosystem-policy-authority-and-consistency` for companion
policy alignment.

Before setup/adoption, release preparation, scoped upgrades or quarterly
maintenance, use `docs/adoption.md#maintaining-the-adopted-stack` and
`docs/baseline-policy.md#dependency-maintenance-means-completed-migration`.
Compare official releases across families, verify compatibility, preserve
project choices, and record exact provenance, rollout/rollback and discovery
evidence. Required stale or unknown freshness blocks adoption and release
acceptance. Keep retained older tools conditional with evidence, owner and
dated revisit. Use `gzs-update-dependencies` for maintenance and
`gzs-dependency-risk-audit` for risk review. For optional separate standard and
X-Plane scans or reviewed update PRs, follow
`docs/baseline-policy.md#scheduled-dependency-scanning`. Automatic merging,
publication and native installation require separate authority.

requirement: an old allowed tool family is not proof of currency. Required stale
or unknown freshness blocks strict acceptance; record any explicit owned
compatibility exception as conditional/noncurrent. The adopter retains this
responsibility when composing an upstream maintenance skill. Explain what applies to this product,
what needs reconciliation and what is deferred. If `gzs-update-dependencies`
is actually discovered, compose its template-inventory/review or scoped-update
mode under project policy. Its absence does not prevent reading the release and
following the published runbook; do not claim an undiscovered skill ran.

## Reconcile an authorized upgrade

Follow the target's brownfield-upgrade path. Capture rollback; compare the
original starter-managed content, current project edits and target candidates.
Generate candidates in a disposable directory using the clean target checkout.
Review the actual diff before changing product files. The helper intentionally
refuses different existing records; no force-overwrite or delete-and-reconfigure
shortcut is supplied.

Reconcile the instructions fragment, project policy references, starter
version/full SHA and managed host tables together. Preserve application
dependencies/settings, public behavior, explicit lane and local guidance.
If the reviewed release supplies `gz-starter verify`, use its existing-adopter
migration in `docs/adoption-workflow.md#configure-the-adopter-verifier` to
review the separate tool pin, lock, hook, CI and stale requirements together.
Preserve coverage and runtime-design approval, then run the adopter's own gate.
Do not overwrite existing AGENTS with a generated example or hand-edit uv.lock.
Leave native caches to their manager; a template change does not automatically
authorize plugin activation. Backplane remains subject to its readiness rule.

Execute the target's applicable migration, analysis and artifact checks. Keep
lane, configuration, Python acceptance and native discovery as separate results.
Missing/null lane, required failed/unknown/stale evidence or accepted exceptions
cannot become an unqualified strict-conformance claim. Mark unfinished work as
migration pending. Do not alter the product version or manufacture a major PRD
merely because the independent template version changed.

## Report

Give the checked date; old and target starter versions/full SHAs; release link;
policy delta; adopt/defer decision; changed files; observed checks and remaining
migration/readiness gaps; and rollback reference. A review must clearly state
that no update was applied. An applied upgrade must distinguish updated
configuration from completed conformance. Never call the whole stack current
based only on the template. Do not publish releases or notify other adopters
unless the user separately requests those actions.

# Architectural decision policy

This starter policy applies to both lite and heavy adopters and to the starter's
own development. Use the project's existing authorities and suitable ADR
conventions. The starter owns this mandatory binding; gz-skills owns the portable
procedure/template, SP owns feature workflows and Backplane owns its existing
planning/tracking integration. Adopt no GZKit ledger or lifecycle through it.

Source: the [operator-accepted lightweight guidance and sample](https://github.com/wtcis-pvecob/cob_projects/blob/dd1ab883c04e884678ed723959b17c5c364263d1/docs/engineering/proposals/2026-11-07-gz-adr-workflow-discussion.md#final-audience-guidance),
as bound by the approved starter design. Starter distribution follows ADR-0001
(`docs/decisions/ADR-0001-001-qualify-exact-component-combinations.md` in the
canonical starter source identified by the recorded revision):
qualify exact reviewed component combinations; keep independent versions/releases.

## Recognize, reuse and align

During design, implementation and review, inspect applicable decisions and
accepted constraints before introducing consequential choices about ownership,
dependencies, interfaces, persistence, recovery, trust, deployment or operation.
Reuse applicable approved decisions and cite them; do not demand another ADR or
approval for routine work within their scope.

For a new, conflicting or materially replacement choice, explain the choice,
credible alternatives, consequences and material uncertainty. Draft the ADR and
obtain separate explicit human approval of its identified edition before
dependent implementation. A design, plan, green test or release approval does
not substitute. Pause only dependent work, including for choices discovered
mid-implementation; continue independent authorized work. Surface conflicting
authorities rather than selecting an undocumented winner.

Recover existing justification first. Investigate important gaps proportionately;
require neither a new research artifact nor external precedent for every ADR.
Code shows what exists, not necessarily why it was chosen or approved. Disclose
inference and unknown history. Correct implementation drift against an approved
choice; do not rewrite the choice to bless conflicting code.

## Keep the decision and its approval together

Keep the choice, scope, context, credible alternatives, rationale, consequences,
approval metadata and amendment history in the ADR. Include a Confirmation
approach when useful; keep test output, progress and delivery claims in existing
verification/planning records. An optional index only helps locate decisions.

For a new collection, use `ADR-0001-001-title-in-kebab-case.md`: stable unique
decision identity, positive integer edition and descriptive title. Never reuse
an id. Preserve suitable existing conventions through an explicit semantic
mapping, not blanket renaming. The starter's own collection is `docs/decisions/`.
Project instructions must identify the project's actual collection.

Authoritative records use Current or Retired and carry `id`, `title`, `revision`,
`state`, `decision_date`, `revision_date`, `approved_by`, `approved_revision` and
`approval_ref`. Use actual YYYY-MM-DD dates and the authorized human's project
identity. Drafts confer no authority; do not fill approval fields with invented
values or mark an unapproved record Current.

Approval evidence must preserve the actual explicit approval of the identified
edition and its reviewed content. Use a retrievable conversation/review reference
and immutable content reference, or preserve the actual interaction with its
source context, date, identity and exact reviewed bytes/hash. Evidence may be
embedded in the ADR or durably referenced from it; no separate receipt file is
mandatory. Label an agent transcription honestly. A hash/commit identifies
content, while only the actual human response establishes approval. Preserve
the proposal before administrative approval capture and disclose that transition.

## Preserve history and independent evolution

Keep earlier editions retrievable by version history or an existing preserved-
document mechanism. Keep the latest filename as the working ADR and repair
affected links after renames. Approval references retain the reviewed edition.

For editorial changes that preserve the choice, scope and constraints, increment
the edition, update its date/filename and record the previous edition, edit,
editor and existing review/change reference. Preserve the original decision
date and approved revision. Use ordinary documentation review; no architectural
reapproval or additional reviewer is required for a typo. Surface uncertain
meaning rather than calling it editorial. A materially changed choice receives
a new, separately approved ADR.

Retirement requires explicit authority, date, reason and a replacement reference
where applicable. Preserve the record and approval history. Do not disguise
retirement as an editorial amendment. Backfill honestly: distinguish documented
approval, observed code, inferred rationale and unknowns. Disclose unsupported
historical dates as unknown; obtain missing approval now without backdating it.
No blanket historical backfill is required by this binding.

Decisions, requirements, features, designs/plans, evidence, instructions and
releases evolve independently. Links express applicability and constraints,
not one-to-one containment, matching versions or automatic revision cascades.
Recheck affected relationships after changes; amend a record only when its own
meaning/applicability changes. ADR approval adds no data, migration, deployment
or publication permission. Preserve and use existing authority without redundant
requests.

## Access, workflow availability and qualification

Project instructions may identify an immutable source link, a repository-local
policy copy, or both. Record starter version/full SHA, source path and original
content hash for local copies; preserve and review project adaptations. When a
local copy is selected, use it as the identified working policy and retain the
canonical link for comparison. Surface applicable local/source conflicts;
do not silently switch sources or overwrite project changes. If required policy,
procedure or approval content is unreadable, report the gap and withhold affected
completion claims while continuing independent authorized work.

Consult the exact selected gz-skills portable procedure/template when its owning
delivery is verified. Released gz-skills 0.13.0 supplies
`gzs-architectural-decisions` and its template; the source-bound qualification
receipt is `docs/evidence/2026-11-15-adr-combination.md` in the starter. Verify
actual installed/discovered sources before extending its observed scope. Heavy mode uses existing supported
Backplane records; no new approval ledger/service is introduced. When Backplane
is disabled, retain existing planning/review/handoff tools in either lane.

Before adopter propagation, require immutable released companion contributions,
full shared behavioral evaluation plus targeted binding checks (including both
missing-approval stopping and approved-decision continuation), and genuine
internal use/alignment review in all three publishers. Expand affected evaluation
when bindings change shared behavior or expose discrepancies. Record exact
sources, loaded configuration, actual observations and limitations in existing
release evidence. Configuration, metadata and passing helper tests alone prove
none of behavioral compliance, native discovery or approval.

releases.fragment_template:
# Skills-first development stack

Read the project's `AGENTS.md` and linked authorities first. Preserve its
domain rules, decisions, verification commands and app architecture. These
starter requirements are mandatory. Execute the owning workflow and checks,
record evidence, and report unmet requirements and policy-approved exceptions.
Preserve failing results. Verify installed revisions and discovery separately
from configuration.

**Resolve starter references from the source, version and exact SHA in
`.gz-starter/bundle.lock.json`.** Read the named `docs/` sections in that
reviewed starter checkout, or use a project-owned reconciliation with recorded
provenance. If the governing source is unavailable, report the gap and leave
dependent decisions unresolved. Recognize **GZ Starter**, **starter** and
**starter template** as shorthand for `gz-starter`. Preserve canonical IDs in
commands and provenance. Route “update the starter” or “check the starter
template” through `update-gz-template` or `docs/updating.md` in the corresponding
update or review mode. Clarify only if the reference is ambiguous.

Both lanes MUST store starter state in `.gz-starter/`. Before first adoption
or an upgrade, inspect `.skills-first/` for legacy state. Follow
`docs/updating.md#relocate-legacy-starter-state` to review, back up, relocate,
and verify recognized artifacts. Preserve recorded provenance, local edits,
and unrelated content. Resolve linked or dual state before retrying.

**Dependency maintenance MUST complete migration to the latest stable versions
of every in-scope dependency and tool, including new families.** Bare
`gzs-update-dependencies` is update mode. Review-only requires an explicit check,
assessment or no-changes request. Preserve the approved Python families,
product contracts, thresholds and evidenced exceptions in
`docs/baseline-policy.md#dependency-maintenance-means-completed-migration`.
At session start, do one bounded freshness check against official sources using
applicable recent dated evidence, flag stale or unavailable results, and migrate
only in separately authorized maintenance. Follow
`docs/engineering/verification-policy.md#session-start-freshness-is-a-check`.

## Work and verify

**Starter is the outer loop, SP is the inner loop, and gz-skills is supplemental.**
Starter frames objective, authorized scope, requirements and completion. Use
SP's `using-superpowers` for development within those boundaries, gz-skills
`gzs-router` for distinct supplemental engineering needs, and project-owned
skills for project operations. Confirm actual plugin discovery before invoking
upstream workflows. Read
`docs/architecture.md#outer-loop-inner-loop-and-supplemental-disciplines`.

and policy. Keep generic workflows and skills upstream.

freshly, for changed behavior and affected consumers. Keep full checks for
broad/uncertain changes, verification or dependency/workspace changes, and
integration/release checkpoints. Keep affected/focused hook checks and full
checks runnable. Add tests for meaningful defects at the owning seam. Review
diff and references for documentation-only changes and use relevant changed-file,
existing test and invented rendered checks for bounded presentation changes.

This starter supports Python only, in both lite and heavy lanes. At adoption,
select an explicit lane through the pinned gz-skills setup workflow. Missing
or null selection leaves adoption incomplete. Both lanes require the same
applicable Python baseline, SemVer, major-release PRDs and adoption/release
analysis. Follow `docs/adoption-0.5.md` for greenfield adoption, brownfield
first adoption, structural backport or upgrades. Backplane owns requirements tracking, labeling,
release/backlog monitoring, handoffs and lane definitions. Read
https://github.com/tvproductions/superpowers-backplane/blob/main/docs/superpowers-backplane/modes.md
when selecting a lane. Heavy targets SP, Backplane and gz-skills. Keep Backplane
disabled pending readiness and explicit adoption, report that gap, and preserve
existing planning and handoff authority without creating a ledger or gzkit
lifecycle.

[identified ADR policy]({{ADR_POLICY_WORKING_SOURCE}}). Preserve its
[immutable canonical source]({{ADR_POLICY_CANONICAL_URL}}) and the version, full
SHA, content hash and link/local choice in `.gz-starter/bundle.lock.json`.

conflicts. Identify and retain the project's existing ADR collection and reuse
approved entries. Obtain separate explicit human approval of the exact new or
replacement edition before dependent implementation. Continue independent
authorized work. Keep approval evidence and edition history with the ADR.

selected gz-skills `gzs-architectural-decisions` procedure only after verifying
its source and actual discovery. Follow `docs/adoption.md#architectural-decision-policy-access`

version updates and activation separate. Preserve user defaults and installs,
suppress inherited duplicates in project config, and report unsupported scope
without broadening activation. A shared cache grants no activation authority.

revisions and enablement separately, including the outside-project control.

locks and the Python pin independent of the uv executable floor. Follow

explicit boundary for independent host/runtime environments. Reconcile
nonconforming layout and settings while preserving behavior, data and authorities.

configuration, tool/runtime provenance, exact environments, and source-independent

and native discovery separately. Evidenced departures need an owner and revisit.

deployment unit, configuration owner/location, schema, selection/overrides,
permissions, upgrade preservation and any consuming application/host. Use

`docs/engineering/application-foundations.md#warnings-and-informed-departures`

preserving mandatory requirements and approved ADRs.

pre-commit. Use `docs/engineering/verification-policy.md#bootstrap-and-implementation-verification-for-adopters`
for the fixed adopter hook and automatic first-source transition. Keep existing
coverage and workspace or embedded-host gates. Never use pytest. Run applicable deeper analyses, including C901,
at adoption, release acceptance and on demand outside routine hooks/CI. Follow
`docs/engineering/python.md#adoptionrelease-analysis-and-on-demand-hygiene` for
the adopter minimum and `docs/engineering/python.md#adopter-class-cohesion-requirement`

missing, failed or stale result blocks strict acceptance. Apply
`docs/engineering/cognitive-integration.md#starter-wide-qualification-deferral`.

and report conditional acceptance. Missing shared-engine delivery alone neither
blocks progress nor requires an adopter waiver. Revisit at release preparation
and candidate delivery. End the deferral only after independent qualification
and measurement for the actual consumer. Keep Complexipy for defect reproduction.

versioned official documentation and

For pattern and OS-seam work, use `docs/gz-skills-python.md` to find the selected
gz-skills workflows, including `gzs-cross-platform-python`. Preserve the bound
runtime policy, report missing or conflicting evidence, and verify the actual
host separately.

## Version and maintenance decisions

At requirements intake, planning and change closeout, execute
`docs/versioning.md#required-version-decision-procedure`. PRDs guide majors,
selected work and requirements drive minors, and compatible fixes drive patches.
Every major, including 1.0.0, requires a newly written PRD. Keep the existing
release-scope record and classify the complete pending scope. Derive routine
bumps, reuse a valid target and require a finite initial release. Keep metadata,
runtime, lock and changelog mirrors aligned. Missing required PRD, scope or
version evidence blocks the applicable claim. Report baseline → target,
governing work, compatibility, mirror agreement and publication state. Reserve
`0.0.0` for an unpublished bare scaffold. Set `0.1.0` as soon as original
implementation, tests, docs or configuration is added. Preserve published
versions and tags. Keep app, starter and upstream component versions independent.
Use `docs/versioning.md#classify-compatibility-within-the-selected-scope` for
increment rules and `docs/versioning.md#adopter-provenance-and-upgrades` when
reconciling an older lock or upgrading the starter. Use
`docs/versioning.md#ecosystem-policy-authority-and-consistency` for companion
policy alignment.

Before setup/adoption, release preparation, scoped upgrades or quarterly
maintenance, use `docs/adoption.md#maintaining-the-adopted-stack` and
`docs/baseline-policy.md#dependency-maintenance-means-completed-migration`.
Compare official releases across families, verify compatibility, preserve
project choices, and record exact provenance, rollout/rollback and discovery
evidence. Required stale or unknown freshness blocks adoption and release
acceptance. Keep retained older tools conditional with evidence, owner and
dated revisit. Use `gzs-update-dependencies` for maintenance and
`gzs-dependency-risk-audit` for risk review. For optional separate standard and

`docs/baseline-policy.md#scheduled-dependency-scanning`. Automatic merging,
publication and native installation require separate authority.

choice; do not rewrite the choice to bless conflicting code.

## Keep the decision and its approval together

Keep the choice, scope, context, credible alternatives, rationale, consequences,
approval metadata and amendment history in the ADR. Include a Confirmation
approach when useful; keep test output, progress and delivery claims in existing
verification/planning records. An optional index only helps locate decisions.

For a new collection, use `ADR-0001-001-title-in-kebab-case.md`: stable unique
decision identity, positive integer edition and descriptive title. Never reuse
an id. Preserve suitable existing conventions through an explicit semantic
mapping, not blanket renaming. The starter's own collection is `docs/decisions/`.
Project instructions must identify the project's actual collection.

Authoritative records use Current or Retired and carry `id`, `title`, `revision`,
`state`, `decision_date`, `revision_date`, `approved_by`, `approved_revision` and
`approval_ref`. Use actual YYYY-MM-DD dates and the authorized human's project
identity. Drafts confer no authority; do not fill approval fields with invented
values or mark an unapproved record Current.

Approval evidence must preserve the actual explicit approval of the identified
edition and its reviewed content. Use a retrievable conversation/review reference
and immutable content reference, or preserve the actual interaction with its
source context, date, identity and exact reviewed bytes/hash. Evidence may be
embedded in the ADR or durably referenced from it; no separate receipt file is
mandatory. Label an agent transcription honestly. A hash/commit identifies
content, while only the actual human response establishes approval. Preserve
the proposal before administrative approval capture and disclose that transition.

## Preserve history and independent evolution

Keep earlier editions retrievable by version history or an existing preserved-
document mechanism. Keep the latest filename as the working ADR and repair
affected links after renames. Approval references retain the reviewed edition.

For editorial changes that preserve the choice, scope and constraints, increment
the edition, update its date/filename and record the previous edition, edit,
editor and existing review/change reference. Preserve the original decision
date and approved revision. Use ordinary documentation review; no architectural
reapproval or additional reviewer is required for a typo. Surface uncertain
meaning rather than calling it editorial. A materially changed choice receives
a new, separately approved ADR.

Retirement requires explicit authority, date, reason and a replacement reference
where applicable. Preserve the record and approval history. Do not disguise
retirement as an editorial amendment. Backfill honestly: distinguish documented
approval, observed code, inferred rationale and unknowns. Disclose unsupported
historical dates as unknown; obtain missing approval now without backdating it.
No blanket historical backfill is required by this binding.

Decisions, requirements, features, designs/plans, evidence, instructions and
releases evolve independently. Links express applicability and constraints,
not one-to-one containment, matching versions or automatic revision cascades.
Recheck affected relationships after changes; amend a record only when its own
meaning/applicability changes. ADR approval adds no data, migration, deployment
or publication permission. Preserve and use existing authority without redundant
requests.

## Access, workflow availability and qualification

Project instructions may identify an immutable source link, a repository-local
policy copy, or both. Record starter version/full SHA, source path and original
content hash for local copies; preserve and review project adaptations. When a
local copy is selected, use it as the identified working policy and retain the
canonical link for comparison. Surface applicable local/source conflicts;
do not silently switch sources or overwrite project changes. If required policy,
procedure or approval content is unreadable, report the gap and withhold affected
completion claims while continuing independent authorized work.

Consult the exact selected gz-skills portable procedure/template when its owning
delivery is verified. Released gz-skills 0.13.0 supplies
`gzs-architectural-decisions` and its template; the source-bound qualification
receipt is `docs/evidence/2026-11-15-adr-combination.md` in the starter. Verify
actual installed/discovered sources before extending its observed scope. Heavy mode uses existing supported
Backplane records; no new approval ledger/service is introduced. When Backplane
is disabled, retain existing planning/review/handoff tools in either lane.

Before adopter propagation, require immutable released companion contributions,
full shared behavioral evaluation plus targeted binding checks (including both
missing-approval stopping and approved-decision continuation), and genuine
internal use/alignment review in all three publishers. Expand affected evaluation
when bindings change shared behavior or expose discrepancies. Record exact
sources, loaded configuration, actual observations and limitations in existing
release evidence. Configuration, metadata and passing helper tests alone prove
none of behavioral compliance, native discovery or approval.

releases.fragment_template:
# Skills-first development stack

Read the project's `AGENTS.md` and linked authorities first. Preserve its
domain rules, decisions, verification commands and app architecture. These
starter requirements are mandatory. Execute the owning workflow and checks,
record evidence, and report unmet requirements and policy-approved exceptions.
Preserve failing results. Verify installed revisions and discovery separately
from configuration.

**Resolve starter references from the source, version and exact SHA in
`.gz-starter/bundle.lock.json`.** Read the named `docs/` sections in that
reviewed starter checkout, or use a project-owned reconciliation with recorded
provenance. If the governing source is unavailable, report the gap and leave
dependent decisions unresolved. Recognize **GZ Starter**, **starter** and
**starter template** as shorthand for `gz-starter`. Preserve canonical IDs in
commands and provenance. Route “update the starter” or “check the starter
template” through `update-gz-template` or `docs/updating.md` in the corresponding
update or review mode. Clarify only if the reference is ambiguous.

Both lanes MUST store starter state in `.gz-starter/`. Before first adoption
or an upgrade, inspect `.skills-first/` for legacy state. Follow
`docs/updating.md#relocate-legacy-starter-state` to review, back up, relocate,
and verify recognized artifacts. Preserve recorded provenance, local edits,
and unrelated content. Resolve linked or dual state before retrying.

**Dependency maintenance MUST complete migration to the latest stable versions
of every in-scope dependency and tool, including new families.** Bare
`gzs-update-dependencies` is update mode. Review-only requires an explicit check,
assessment or no-changes request. Preserve the approved Python families,
product contracts, thresholds and evidenced exceptions in
`docs/baseline-policy.md#dependency-maintenance-means-completed-migration`.
At session start, do one bounded freshness check against official sources using
applicable recent dated evidence, flag stale or unavailable results, and migrate
only in separately authorized maintenance. Follow
`docs/engineering/verification-policy.md#session-start-freshness-is-a-check`.

## Work and verify

**Starter is the outer loop, SP is the inner loop, and gz-skills is supplemental.**
Starter frames objective, authorized scope, requirements and completion. Use
SP's `using-superpowers` for development within those boundaries, gz-skills
`gzs-router` for distinct supplemental engineering needs, and project-owned
skills for project operations. Confirm actual plugin discovery before invoking
upstream workflows. Read
`docs/architecture.md#outer-loop-inner-loop-and-supplemental-disciplines`.
The starter owns only `update-gz-template`, its helper, configuration, provenance
and policy. Keep generic workflows and skills upstream.

Use direct `git` and `gh` commands. Use Python for substantive processing through
`uv run --locked python`, honoring the exact managed pin and supported uv.
Follow SP verification-before-completion and
`docs/engineering/verification-policy.md`. Run each selected command in full,
freshly, for changed behavior and affected consumers. Keep full checks for
broad/uncertain changes, verification or dependency/workspace changes, and
integration/release checkpoints. Keep affected/focused hook checks and full
checks runnable. Add tests for meaningful defects at the owning seam. Review
diff and references for documentation-only changes and use relevant changed-file,
existing test and invented rendered checks for bounded presentation changes.
Cite dated, input-matched historical evidence as such. Repeat affected checks
when inputs or risk change and record scope and limits.

## Adoption, decisions and native scope

This starter supports Python only, in both lite and heavy lanes. At adoption,
select an explicit lane through the pinned gz-skills setup workflow. Missing
or null selection leaves adoption incomplete. Both lanes require the same
applicable Python baseline, SemVer, major-release PRDs and adoption/release
analysis. Follow `docs/adoption-0.5.md` for greenfield adoption, brownfield
first adoption, structural backport or upgrades. Backplane owns requirements tracking, labeling,
release/backlog monitoring, handoffs and lane definitions. Read
https://github.com/tvproductions/superpowers-backplane/blob/main/docs/superpowers-backplane/modes.md
when selecting a lane. Heavy targets SP, Backplane and gz-skills. Keep Backplane
disabled pending readiness and explicit adoption, report that gap, and preserve
existing planning and handoff authority without creating a ledger or gzkit
lifecycle.

During design, execution and review in either lane, follow the
[identified ADR policy]({{ADR_POLICY_WORKING_SOURCE}}). Preserve its
[immutable canonical source]({{ADR_POLICY_CANONICAL_URL}}) and the version, full
SHA, content hash and link/local choice in `.gz-starter/bundle.lock.json`.
Honor the selected working copy, preserve local adaptations and report source
conflicts. Identify and retain the project's existing ADR collection and reuse
approved entries. Obtain separate explicit human approval of the exact new or
replacement edition before dependent implementation. Continue independent
authorized work. Keep approval evidence and edition history with the ADR.
General spec, plan, test or release approval does not approve an ADR. Use the
selected gz-skills `gzs-architectural-decisions` procedure only after verifying
its source and actual discovery. Follow `docs/adoption.md#architectural-decision-policy-access`
during ADR policy adoption or reconciliation.

Install and activate only at repository/project scope. Keep installation,
version updates and activation separate. Preserve user defaults and installs,
suppress inherited duplicates in project config, and report unsupported scope
without broadening activation. A shared cache grants no activation authority.
Before adoption, brownfield repair or updates, follow
`docs/adoption.md#repository-owned-installation-and-brownfield-repair` and
`docs/adoption.md#updates-and-rollback`. Preview, review and apply `localize` for
activation repair. Use `configure --host` for full adoption. Verify installed
revisions and enablement separately, including the outside-project control.
Codex CLI 0.166.0 `plugin add` enables user-wide. Do not use it for project
installation, updates or reinstalls. For OpenCode 2.2.0 project
commands, use the reviewed starter's `uv run --locked gz-starter run-opencode
--project <root> -- <native arguments>`. Read `docs/adoption.md#opencode` for its
scope and actual discovery checks.

## Python baseline and configuration

Use uv-managed Python N-1 (currently 3.14.x) and the 3.12.x XPPython3 host
exception. Verify the latest compatible patch in the approved family against
official sources at setup/adoption, release preparation and maintenance. Pin it
exactly in `.python-version` and CI. Test the embedded runtime separately.
Follow `docs/baseline-policy.md#allowed-python-families`. Keep uv compatibility
minimum-only, record CI's exact tested uv separately, and let supported callers
use their actual version with recorded provenance. Keep exact package/backend
locks and the Python pin independent of the uv executable floor. Follow
`docs/baseline-policy.md#uv-executable-compatibility`.

For Python work read `docs/engineering/python.md`. Meet
`docs/engineering/astral-alignment.md` and complete
`docs/engineering/astral-acceptance.md` at adoption and affected reconciliation,
using its worked migrations. Use `src/` packaging, uv_build for pure Python,
installed imports, entry points for apps and `py.typed` for typed libraries.
Centralize shared settings in root `pyproject.toml`, commit `uv.lock` and ignore
`.venv`. For multi-package work, apply
`docs/engineering/astral-alignment.md#workspaces` before changing workspace
structure. Use one root lock/environment and explicit member edges. Require an
explicit boundary for independent host/runtime environments. Reconcile
nonconforming layout and settings while preserving behavior, data and authorities.
Configuration-only work reports remaining refactoring. Verify effective
configuration, tool/runtime provenance, exact environments, and source-independent
builds and clean installed behavior. Record configuration, Python acceptance
and native discovery separately. Evidenced departures need an owner and revisit.

At adoption and when defining or changing a product's deployment or
configuration boundary, apply ADR-0002, `docs/project-configuration.md` and
`docs/engineering/application-foundations.md` in both lanes. Identify the
deployment unit, configuration owner/location, schema, selection/overrides,
permissions, upgrade preservation and any consuming application/host. Use
`settings.json` for operator-managed runtime settings, keep packaging/tool
settings in `pyproject.toml` and pass validated values to domain code. Reject
supplied or resolved paths containing spaces before reading content or writing.
Preserve data and settings during migration and verify actual consumer behavior.
For architectural warnings or naming/layout advice, read
`docs/engineering/application-foundations.md#warnings-and-informed-departures`
and `docs/engineering/naming-and-layout.md`. Record informed departures once,
preserving mandatory requirements and approved ADRs.

Keep routine hooks limited to locked Ruff check/format, ty and unittest through
pre-commit. Use `docs/engineering/verification-policy.md#bootstrap-and-implementation-verification-for-adopters`
for the fixed adopter hook and automatic first-source transition. Keep existing
coverage and workspace or embedded-host gates. Never use pytest. Run applicable deeper analyses, including C901,
at adoption, release acceptance and on demand outside routine hooks/CI. Follow
`docs/engineering/python.md#adoptionrelease-analysis-and-on-demand-hygiene` for
the adopter minimum and `docs/engineering/python.md#adopter-class-cohesion-requirement`
for project-owned cohesion pins, runtime proofs and reporting. A required
missing, failed or stale result blocks strict acceptance. Apply
`docs/engineering/cognitive-integration.md#starter-wide-qualification-deferral`.
Record **DEFERRED / measurement UNKNOWN**, retain ceiling 15 and all other checks,
and report conditional acceptance. Missing shared-engine delivery alone neither
blocks progress nor requires an adopter waiver. Revisit at release preparation
and candidate delivery. End the deferral only after independent qualification
and measurement for the actual consumer. Keep Complexipy for defect reproduction.

At adoption, Python-family changes, design, review and scoped maintenance, use
versioned official documentation and
`docs/engineering/python.md#version-aware-design` to assess idioms, stdlib changes
and deprecations. Record concrete benefits, risks and adopt/defer decisions.
For pattern and OS-seam work, use `docs/gz-skills-python.md` to find the selected
gz-skills workflows, including `gzs-cross-platform-python`. Preserve the bound
runtime policy, report missing or conflicting evidence, and verify the actual
host separately.

## Version and maintenance decisions

At requirements intake, planning and change closeout, execute
`docs/versioning.md#required-version-decision-procedure`. PRDs guide majors,
selected work and requirements drive minors, and compatible fixes drive patches.
Every major, including 1.0.0, requires a newly written PRD. Keep the existing
release-scope record and classify the complete pending scope. Derive routine
bumps, reuse a valid target and require a finite initial release. Keep metadata,
runtime, lock and changelog mirrors aligned. Missing required PRD, scope or
version evidence blocks the applicable claim. Report baseline → target,
governing work, compatibility, mirror agreement and publication state. Reserve
`0.0.0` for an unpublished bare scaffold. Set `0.1.0` as soon as original
implementation, tests, docs or configuration is added. Preserve published
versions and tags. Keep app, starter and upstream component versions independent.
Use `docs/versioning.md#classify-compatibility-within-the-selected-scope` for
increment rules and `docs/versioning.md#adopter-provenance-and-upgrades` when
reconciling an older lock or upgrading the starter. Use
`docs/versioning.md#ecosystem-policy-authority-and-consistency` for companion
policy alignment.

Before setup/adoption, release preparation, scoped upgrades or quarterly
maintenance, use `docs/adoption.md#maintaining-the-adopted-stack` and
`docs/baseline-policy.md#dependency-maintenance-means-completed-migration`.
Compare official releases across families, verify compatibility, preserve
project choices, and record exact provenance, rollout/rollback and discovery
evidence. Required stale or unknown freshness blocks adoption and release
acceptance. Keep retained older tools conditional with evidence, owner and
dated revisit. Use `gzs-update-dependencies` for maintenance and
`gzs-dependency-risk-audit` for risk review. For optional separate standard and
X-Plane scans or reviewed update PRs, follow
`docs/baseline-policy.md#scheduled-dependency-scanning`. Automatic merging,
publication and native installation require separate authority.
releases.update_skill_template:
---
name: update-gz-template
description: Check or update a project's adopted gz-starter template, explain released policy changes, and reconcile migration guidance. Use for starter-version reviews and template upgrades, rather than general package or plugin updates.
---

# Update the GZ template

Help an existing adopter consume released template policy without replacing its
product. The canonical repository is
`https://github.com/tvproductions/gz-starter`. This is a narrow guide
to its maintained adoption instructions, not another dependency updater.

## Establish the request and current adoption

Read the target project's AGENTS and existing authorities. Confirm its root and
dirty state. Preserve unrelated work. Inspect `.skills-first/` and `.gz-starter/`
and their `bundle.lock.json`, `architectural-decisions.md`, and `settings.toml`
entries by metadata before opening either record. Read a reviewed regular lock
for the starter repository, version/full SHA, and component selections.
Recognized legacy, linked, or dual state requires reviewed reconciliation. Follow
`docs/updating.md#relocate-legacy-starter-state` in the target release. Keep review
mode read-only. During an authorized migration, preserve unrelated content and
recorded provenance. Report a directory-only move as relocation with template
reconciliation pending when the managed files still differ.
Read `.gz-skills/settings.json` for the explicit lite/heavy choice. Absent or
legacy provenance stays unknown; do not infer it from today's version label.
Read the lock's selected native `host`; legacy records without it use Codex.
Use that host's repository-owned settings. For activation-only repair, follow
the reviewed starter's `localize --host` procedure; do not rewrite adoption
provenance or uninstall existing global copies. Installation, version updates
and enablement MUST remain separate. Project commands MUST preserve local scope.

A request to check or explain updates authorizes review only. Do not sync,
resolve, install or modify the adopter in review mode. A request to upgrade
authorizes the scoped template reconciliation and necessary verification; use
that authorization without asking again for routine migration steps. Keep
runtime/tool/plugin refreshes separate unless required by the reviewed target
policy or included in the user's request. For broader dependency/tool maintenance,
follow the starter's mandatory
`docs/baseline-policy.md#dependency-maintenance-means-completed-migration` binding:
maintenance and bare `gzs-update-dependencies` invocations require completing the
most current stable migration across newer families and verification, overriding
the portable skill's review-only default here. Only explicit check, freshness,
assessment or no-changes requests are review-only. Do not end a broader maintenance
request with this narrow template assessment or an offer to apply. Preserve
Python N-1/embedded-host policy, product requirements and demonstrated, owned,
dated compatibility exceptions. With no adoption record, identify
first adoption and follow the starter's greenfield/brownfield entry instead of
pretending this is an upgrade. A gzkit project retains its separate ecosystem.

## Find the released target and its instructions

When the target includes application foundations, review
docs/project-configuration.md, docs/engineering/application-foundations.md and
docs/engineering/naming-and-layout.md with the adopter's existing deployment and
settings contract. Inventory formats, variable names, path bases, credentials,
data and automation; preview migration and preserve working inputs. Do not
overwrite settings or infer a shared runtime-loader dependency. Explain the
settings.json default, startup boundary, explicit configuration owner and
space-free path requirement, recording informed departures in existing authority.
Verify the actual application's positive/negative behavior and installed
preservation; starter fixture/configuration results cannot qualify that adopter.

Query the canonical repository's live stable releases with direct `gh` commands.
Use direct `git` commands for repository operations. Do not wrap routine CLI
calls in Python; substantive Python processing must use the prescribed locked,
uv-managed environment. For example:

```bash
gh api repos/tvproductions/gz-starter/releases/latest --jq '{tag_name,html_url,published_at}'
```

Respect an explicitly requested published target. A failed query is UNKNOWN,
not proof of no updates. Distinguish a release from newer main; a version string
alone proves neither source identity nor publication. Use a separate clean
checkout of the selected tag, resolve `TAG^{commit}` to its full SHA, and compare
with HEAD and the target manifest before applying. Never use the adopter's own
HEAD as starter provenance.

Read the selected release notes, intervening changelogs, `docs/versioning.md`,
`docs/baseline-policy.md` and `docs/adoption-workflow.md` at that exact target.
Follow the current runbook linked there; do not freeze a historical filename or
copy its whole procedure into this skill. Release 0.5.0 links
`docs/adoption-0.5.md`; future releases may link a successor. If a tool cannot
fetch the required instructions, report that gap rather than guess the migration.
When present at the target, `docs/updating.md` owns the canonical update and
older-adopter bootstrap method. Reconcile this project skill along with the
other managed content; adding it alone does not upgrade the adopted baseline.

Compare policy changes as well as pins. Enforce the target's latest-tooling
requirement: an old allowed tool family is not proof of currency. Required stale
or unknown freshness blocks strict acceptance; record any explicit owned
compatibility exception as conditional/noncurrent. The adopter retains this
responsibility when composing an upstream maintenance skill. Explain what applies to this product,
what needs reconciliation and what is deferred. If `gzs-update-dependencies`
is actually discovered, compose its template-inventory/review or scoped-update
mode under project policy. Its absence does not prevent reading the release and
following the published runbook; do not claim an undiscovered skill ran.

## Reconcile an authorized upgrade

Follow the target's brownfield-upgrade path. Capture rollback; compare the
original starter-managed content, current project edits and target candidates.
Generate candidates in a disposable directory using the clean target checkout.
Review the actual diff before changing product files. The helper intentionally
refuses different existing records; no force-overwrite or delete-and-reconfigure
shortcut is supplied.

Reconcile the instructions fragment, project policy references, starter
version/full SHA and managed host tables together. Preserve application
dependencies/settings, public behavior, explicit lane and local guidance.
If the reviewed release supplies `gz-starter verify`, use its existing-adopter
migration in `docs/adoption-workflow.md#configure-the-adopter-verifier` to
review the separate tool pin, lock, hook, CI and stale requirements together.
Preserve coverage and runtime-design approval, then run the adopter's own gate.
Do not overwrite existing AGENTS with a generated example or hand-edit uv.lock.
Leave native caches to their manager; a template change does not automatically
authorize plugin activation. Backplane remains subject to its readiness rule.

Execute the target's applicable migration, analysis and artifact checks. Keep
lane, configuration, Python acceptance and native discovery as separate results.
Missing/null lane, required failed/unknown/stale evidence or accepted exceptions
cannot become an unqualified strict-conformance claim. Mark unfinished work as
migration pending. Do not alter the product version or manufacture a major PRD
merely because the independent template version changed.

## Report

Give the checked date; old and target starter versions/full SHAs; release link;
policy delta; adopt/defer decision; changed files; observed checks and remaining
migration/readiness gaps; and rollback reference. A review must clearly state
that no update was applied. An applied upgrade must distinguish updated
configuration from completed conformance. Never call the whole stack current
based only on the template. Do not publish releases or notify other adopters
unless the user separately requests those actions.
